the le galist keeps score, the lover doesn’t. love thinks of how it might give more, do more, dem onstrate love more fully. there are many examples of people who are poor in pocket, but rich in love. more than anything else, god wants to be in a love relationship with you (gospel). he wants your love more than your obedience or service! but if love god, you will do those other things. so, are you a legalist or a lover, alive or dead in how you live your faith? monday is the feast of all souls . a plenary indulgence will apply for the 1st & 2nd november and also from the 1st to the 8th november. plenary indulgence the church offers a plenary indulgence during these days for those who have died and who are awaiting purification – we refer to these as souls in purgatory. a plenary indulgence is a remission of the punishment due to s ins and is gained by our prayers for the dead. it may be gained in two ways: 1. once by visiting a church between midday november 1st and midnight november 2nd and there say one our father and the apostles creed and also pray the pope’s intentions. 2. once each day by visiting a cemetery from midday november 1st to november 8th and praying for the dead. both these indulgences require that the sacraments of holy communion and reconciliation be received within twenty days. remembering our dead all souls’ day invites us to pause, remember and reflect, not with fear or despair, but with hope and love. it is a quiet sacred time in the christian calen dar when we turn our hearts toward those who have gone before us. it reminds us that death is not an end, but a rite of passage and that love, especially in christ, does not end at the grave. we remember the ordinary faithful, our parents, friends, neighbours, strangers who lived, struggled and hoped just like we do. some may have died suddenly, others after long goodbyes. some we knew intimately; others we never met. yet we are all connected in the mystery of the communion of saints, the living, the dead, and those yet to come. on this day, we pray for the souls in purgatory, trusting that our prayers, united with the mercy of god, help them on their journ ey towards full union with him. our prayers are acts of love, and reminders that they are not for gotten. all souls’ day gently confronts us with our own mortality. but instead o f leading us to fear, it calls us to live well with compassion, humility, forgiveness, and faith so that when our time comes, we too may be welcomed into the fullness of god's presence. prayer on visiting the grave of a loved one father in heaven, as we stand before the resting place of our beloved , we remember the gift they were and continue to be to each of us here present. we thank you for their life, the love they shared with us, and we pray that they are with you now, enjo ying the fullness of eternal life. comfort us in our sadness, strengthen us with your hope, until we are united with them again in the love of christ and we are with you and our loved one forever. amen. cemetery prayers sunday 1st november - prayers will be offered in st. fanahan’s cemetery adjoining the parish church immediately after the 11.30am mass and at brigown cemetery at 2.30pm. sunday 8th november - prayers will be offered in the presentation convent cemetery immediately after the 11.30am mass and in marshalstown cemetery at 2.30pm.

all saints we can often get side-tracked by canonised saints a nd forget the saints that we, ourselves, have known. these were people who did the ‘ordinary’ ext raordinarily well; who brought us untold joy by simply being, caring, loving, by lives poured in the service of others. they were people who loved life, who made us laugh and laughed themselves till their sides hurt; who affirmed us and others; who built up rather than tore down; they also thought of the world as essentially a good place and rejoiced in it, while being fully aw are of their own shortcomings. thomas merton once wrote: ‘forme, to be a saint is to be myself. ’ masses during the week in the parish church – 26th to 30th october 2026 monday (bank holiday): mass: 11am tuesday to friday: rosary: 9:30am mass: 10am friday: divine mercy: 3pm. confessions 31st october 2026 confessions in parish church: saturday 12 noon parish masses on sunday 1st november 2026 – feast of all saints parish church – vigil 7:30pm; 8:30am and 11:30am. killacluig; – 10:00am. please note mass times are displayed on church noticeboards. live streaming of masses in the parish church, please use the following link:

saints feast days for the coming week wednesday, 28th october - simon & jude: the teaching of the apostles is the living gospel for all to hear. their authority comes from their fidelity to christ and his message. st. jude i s the patron saint of useless causes. thursday, 29th october – st. colman : he hailed from kilmacduagh, co. galway. son of a chieftain named duagh. hermit in arranmore where he built two churches. his reputation for holiness attracted too much attention, so he retreated to the woods of burren in 592 to live in isolation. in 610, on land donated by king guaire of connacht , he founded a monastery which became the center of the diocese of kilmacduagh . he reluctantly served as the house’s first abbot, the dioceses first bishop. saturday, 31st october - blessed dominic collins: was born around 1566 in the town of youghal, co cork. in 1598, after a military career, he entered the society of jesus as a brother. he returned to ireland in 1601, but on the 16th june 1602, was captured by the english who tried in vain to make him abjure his faith. condemned to death, he was hanged in his native town on 31st october 1602. sunday, 1st november - all saints: ‘the ultimate object of veneration of the saints is the glory of god and the sanctification of humanity by conforming one’s life fully to the divine will and by imitating the virtue of those who were pre- existent disciples of the lord.’ monday, 2nd november - all souls: ‘indeed the church in its pilgrim members, from the very earliest days of the christian faith, has honoured with great res pect the memory of the dead; and ‘because it is a holy and a wholesome thought to pray for the dead that they may be loosed from thei r sins.’ (2 mac: 12-46), she offers her suffrages for them. these consist, primarily, in the celebration of the eucharist, and prayers for the dead, alms , deeds, works of mercy, and the application of indulgences to the souls of the faithful departed’. matthew 22:34-40 when the pharisees heard that jesus had silenced the sadducees they got together and, to disconcert him , one of them put a question, ‘master, which is the greatest commandment of the law?
jesus said, ‘you must love the lord your god with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.
this is the greatest and the first commandment.
the second r esembles it: you must love your neighbour as yourself.

on these two commandments hang the whole law, and the prophets also .’.’ responsorial psalm . 17(18):2-4,47,51 i love you, lord, my strength. “you must love’” another group from the leadership of the jews seek to catch jesus out, the sadducees.
jesus answers their question correctly by saying th at love of god comes before all else, how ever he also adds the second commandment, love your neig hbour as yourself.
in this way jesus is telling us that to love god is to love one another.
we cannot separate them. "if anyone says , 'i love god,' and yet hates his brother or sister, is a liar.
for the person who does not love his brothe r or sister whom he has seen cannot love god whom he has not seen.". (1john 4:20).

this love is not to be just words or mere talk but to be practical as we hear in the first reading for this sunday from the book of exodus. “ you must not molest the stranger or oppress him, you lived as strangers in the land of egypt.
you must not be harsh with the widow, or with the orphan ” (ex22:20) memory is a very important part of our lives, it is important to recall who we are and where we come from.
to love the stranger for the israelites is to remember that they were strangers in othe r lands in the past, and they know what it is not to belong.
god has called us all into his family, we belong to him.

while we can all be comfortable in belonging to a particular people and place and be wary of strangers, of people different to ourselves w hich can lead to segregation, racism, blaming stranger for everything, we as christians know that we are up of people from every nation and culture.
our belonging is in christ and thus we are called to love one another as jesus loves us. welcoming to the stranger and to those in need.
